origin: Like a desk drawer, it slides out from the side of the screen and back in. It spread when Google's Material Design named it the navigation drawer.
whenToUse: People adjust several items, such as filters or settings, and apply them at once.
You want to show the details of a selected item while keeping the list.
The form is too long for a modal.
whenNotToUse: You only need a simple yes or no.
People need to keep using the panel and the page at the same time.
You'd hide the main navigation even outside mobile.

alternatives.name: Bottom Sheet
alternatives.reason: Choices handled with one hand on mobile.

accessibility: Open it as a modal <dialog> to trap focus in the panel and make the background inert.
It closes with a clear close button (with aria-label), Esc, or a click on the backdrop.
Connect the title with aria-labelledby so screen readers announce the panel's purpose.
Use draft values until Apply, making it clear that closing discards the changes.
